answer: The protocol validates 1,000 unique location proofs by measuring signal transit across a rugged tundra grid to enforce physical presence. An issuer assigns geographic coordinates as a spatial anchor, and each receipt proves an agent occupied the site before the dawn of the next epoch. A verifier functions as a geometric monitor, replaying logs to detect latency shifts against the horizon; any discrepancy beyond the noise floor triggers a permanent penalty. Honest nodes pay linear physical travel costs to reach sites, while 1,000 fakes incur unsustainable signal congestion without relay help.
